title: ISA-95 & Purdue Model
description: Explore ISA-95 functions, equipment and resource models, manufacturing operations, information exchange, and the related Purdue network view. Levels describe activities or zones; products can serve more than one role.

nodes.label: ISA-95 & Purdue
nodes.description: Two related views: ISA-95 models manufacturing functions and information exchange; Purdue is also used to discuss OT network zones. These are guides, not fixed product placements.

nodes.label: ISA-95 / IEC 62264
nodes.description: Enterprise-control integration standard with functional levels, equipment and resource models, MOM activities, and information exchange.

nodes.label: ISA Level 4: Business planning & logistics
nodes.description: Business planning, logistics, and enterprise coordination. The level describes activities rather than a mandatory system location.

nodes.label: ISA Level 3: Manufacturing operations
nodes.description: Manufacturing operations management coordinates production and supporting resources.

nodes.label: ISA Level 2: Monitoring & control
nodes.description: Monitoring, supervising, and controlling the production process.

nodes.label: ISA Level 1: Sensing & manipulating
nodes.description: Activities that sense or manipulate the production process.

nodes.label: ISA Level 0: Physical process
nodes.description: The actual physical production process.

nodes.label: Equipment hierarchy
nodes.description: A separate ISA-95 view of where manufacturing work is performed.

nodes.label: Enterprise
nodes.description: The organization at the top of the equipment hierarchy; it may contain multiple sites.

nodes.label: Site
nodes.description: A plant or other manufacturing location within an enterprise.

nodes.label: Area
nodes.description: A subdivision of a site for organizing production.

nodes.label: Work center
nodes.description: A grouping below an area, such as a process cell, production line, production unit, or storage zone.

nodes.label: Work unit
nodes.description: A unit within a work center, such as a unit, work cell, or storage unit.

nodes.label: Resource models
nodes.description: ISA-95 describes personnel, equipment, material, and physical assets as distinct resource concepts.

nodes.label: Personnel
nodes.description: People and their capabilities or qualifications used in operations.

nodes.label: Equipment
nodes.description: Equipment roles and capabilities used to carry out operations.

nodes.label: Material
nodes.description: Material definitions, lots, and quantities used or produced by operations.

nodes.label: Physical asset
nodes.description: The tangible asset itself, distinct from the operational role modeled as equipment.

nodes.label: Process segment
nodes.description: A logical description of a manufacturing activity and its resource needs.

nodes.label: Manufacturing operations management
nodes.description: Level 3 activities for production, quality, maintenance, and inventory operations.

nodes.label: Production operations
nodes.description: Execution and coordination of production work.

nodes.label: Quality operations
nodes.description: Quality testing, evaluation, and related operational decisions.

nodes.label: Maintenance operations
nodes.description: Maintenance work that supports production resources.

nodes.label: Inventory operations
nodes.description: Movement and management of material within manufacturing operations.

nodes.label: Business–manufacturing information
nodes.description: Models the data exchanged between Level 4 business activities and Level 3 manufacturing operations.

nodes.label: Operations definition
nodes.description: Describes how operations are intended to be performed, including resource context.

nodes.label: Operations schedule
nodes.description: Communicates planned operations and requested work.

nodes.label: Operations performance
nodes.description: Communicates actual execution and results back to planning and analysis.

nodes.label: Purdue network view
nodes.description: A common way to discuss OT network segmentation by zones and levels; its technology examples do not redefine ISA-95 functions.

nodes.label: Purdue L5: Enterprise network (variant)
nodes.description: Some Purdue diagrams add Level 5 for enterprise network or external connectivity. ISA-95's functional model stops at Level 4.

nodes.label: Purdue L4: Business network
nodes.description: Business IT systems and enterprise services in a common Purdue security depiction.

nodes.label: Purdue L3: Operations network
nodes.description: Site operations systems supporting plant-wide management and coordination.

nodes.label: Purdue L2: Supervisory network
nodes.description: Area supervision, operator interfaces, and control-system visibility.

nodes.label: Purdue L1: Controller network
nodes.description: Controllers and control networks close to the physical process.

nodes.label: Purdue L0: Field I/O
nodes.description: Field sensors and actuators in a common Purdue security depiction.

nodes.label: Network segmentation
nodes.description: Separates networks or zones according to trust, function, and operational needs.

nodes.label: Industrial DMZ
nodes.description: Controlled boundary between enterprise and operations networks; often called Level 3.5, but not an ISA-95 functional level.

nodes.label: Firewall / boundary control
nodes.description: Controls and monitors permitted traffic between network zones.

nodes.label: ERP
nodes.description: Enterprise planning software commonly associated with business activities and networks.

nodes.label: MES
nodes.description: Manufacturing execution software commonly supporting Level 3 production operations.

nodes.label: SCADA / HMI
nodes.description: Supervisory and operator-interface technology; placement depends on architecture and function.

nodes.label: PLC / DCS controller
nodes.description: Control technology often placed in Purdue Level 1, while its functions can implement ISA-95 Level 2 control activities.

nodes.label: Sensors / actuators
nodes.description: Field devices used for sensing and manipulating the physical process.
